candidates.sentence: Neural architecture search researchers already test smoothness with neighbours. The NAS-Bench-101 benchmark calls two networks neighbours when one change separates them, one operation swapped or one connection flipped, and it takes a long random walk to see how well each network's accuracy predicts the next one's. I borrowed the neighbour and the question. For Pokemon one change is a legal move, ability, item, stat alignment, Stat Points or whole Pokemon. Instead of a long walk I take one step from each of 40 starting teams, and I subtract the battle luck I see when the same team is replayed with nothing changed.

facts.claim: NAS-Bench-101 defines closeness by edit distance, where one change flips the operation at a vertex or the presence of an edge, and measures locality with random-walk autocorrelation over a long walk of random changes, citing Weinberger 1990.
facts.source: Ying et al. 2019, NAS-Bench-101, Section 3.3 Locality, https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.09635

facts.claim: The project's measurement takes one step per edit, not a random walk: the size of one edit is the root of the mean squared move of edits minus the mean squared move of unchanged replays, against the team's first score.
40 starting teams, 24 tournament-ready and 16 search-found, each got 18 edits across six kinds and three replays with nothing changed.
The neighbour correlation the project reports is implied by the edit size, 1 minus share squared over 2, so it maps to the idea of random-walk autocorrelation and not to the exact estimator.
facts.source: code/scripts/top50_one_edit.py, function edit_size docstring, and code/docs/ruggedness2.md, section 'Statistics'

facts.claim: Full citation, each field checked against Crossref and the publisher's page. He tested the measure on Kauffman's N-k model.
facts.source: Weinberger, E. 1990. Correlated and uncorrelated fitness landscapes and how to tell the difference. Biological Cybernetics 63(5), 325-336. https://doi.org/10.1007/BF00202749

candidates.sentence: Biologists call this picture a fitness landscape, and the one-edit test comes from it. A team plays the role of a genome, one legal edit plays the role of one mutation, and win rate plays the role of fitness. The question carried over is how well a point's fitness predicts its neighbour's. What changed for Pokemon is that fitness comes from 384 battles, which carry luck, so each starting team is also replayed three times untouched and only the movement beyond that luck counts as the edit.

facts.claim: Weinberger 1990, 'Correlated and uncorrelated fitness landscapes and how to tell the difference', Biological Cybernetics, is the source NAS-Bench-101 cites for random-walk autocorrelation as a measure of locality.
facts.source: Ying et al. 2019, NAS-Bench-101, Section 3.3 and reference list, https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.09635

facts.claim: Each score is a win rate over 384 battles, and each starting team was replayed three times with nothing changed to measure battle luck.
The noise of unchanged replays is subtracted from the edits' squared moves before the size is taken, and a negative remainder is set to zero.
Full citation, each field checked against Crossref and the publisher's page. He tested the measure on Kauffman's N-k model.
facts.source: Weinberger, E. 1990. Correlated and uncorrelated fitness landscapes and how to tell the difference. Biological Cybernetics 63(5), 325-336. https://doi.org/10.1007/BF00202749

candidates.sentence: Combinatorial Bayesian optimisation gave me the yardstick. On its Pest Control benchmark, 25 stations each pick one of five options, four pesticides or none, and two settings are neighbours when exactly one station differs. I ran the same one-step test on Pest Control from random and hill-climbed starting points and divided each step by that benchmark's own spread of scores. Replacing one whole Pokemon on a tournament-ready team moves win rate by 0.65 of the spread between teams, larger than a Pest Control step however that benchmark's spread is counted.

facts.claim: In COMBO's combinatorial graph, two vertices are connected when their choices differ by a single combinatorial choice.
facts.source: Oh et al. 2019, Combinatorial Bayesian Optimization using the Graph Cartesian Product, Section 2.2, https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.00448

facts.claim: Pest Control has 25 variables with 5 categories each: 4 pesticides and the choice of using none.
facts.source: Oh et al. 2019, Supplement Section 4.2.2, https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.00448

facts.claim: The benchmark side uses random starting points and points found by a first-improvement hill climb, with one edit setting one station to another value.

A Pest Control step is 0.14 of that benchmark's spread pooled over both kinds of starting point, and 0.37 and 0.32 when each kind uses its own spread. Decided 2026-11-13: the two kinds of starting point are not pooled, so the step is 0.37 and 0.32 and the pooled 0.14 is not used.
facts.source: notes/artifacts/one-edit-away-explanation-elements/v2/FACTS.md, section 'Reading two, against a benchmark step'

facts.claim: The whole-Pokemon swap on tournament-ready teams is 5.90 points, 0.65 of the 9.04-point spread of true scores between teams.
facts.source: notes/artifacts/one-edit-away-explanation-elements/rerun-readings.json, keys spread_between_teams_points and groups.outside_top50, and code/docs/ruggedness2.md, section 'Reading without the 5-point cutoff'

Answered 2026-11-13: the full citation is Weinberger, E. 1990. Correlated and uncorrelated fitness landscapes and how to tell the difference. Biological Cybernetics 63(5), 325-336. https://doi.org/10.1007/BF00202749. The abstract says his experiments used "a single family of landscapes (Kauffman's 'N-k model')", so the sentence can end "on Kauffman's N-k model of fitness landscapes from evolutionary biology". His measure is "the autocorrelation of fitnesses obtained from a random walk on the landscape", and its value at one step is the correlation between a point and a neighbour one edit away, so your sentence is accurate as written. The full text is behind a paywall, so this rests on the abstract and on NAS-Bench-101, Section 3.3. Report: v2/q-weinberger-citation.md
